Desembargador e presidente do Tribunal de Justiça do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (TJRJ), Couto assumiu interinamente o comando do Palácio Guanabara em 23 de março, após a renúncia de Cláudio Castro e o esgotamento da linha sucessória estadual. Ao fazer um balanço de sua administração, Couto afirmou que a prioridade foi reorganizar a máquina pública e preparar o estado para a transição de governo. “Procurei entregar o Estado apto a ser gerido pelo próximo governador. Reduzimos a máquina, valorizamos os servidores de carreira e buscamos fazer uma transição adequada, sempre respeitando a população”, disse ao Valor após votar. Aos 62 anos, Couto tem uma trajetória de mais de três décadas na magistratura. As ocorrências foram registradas nos Estados da Bahia, Minas Gerais, Roraima, Acre, Distrito Federal, Rondônia, Amapá e Paraíba. Entre os principais crimes apurados estão a propaganda eleitoral irregular e a corrupção eleitoral, especialmente a compra de votos. title: Why the U.S. Navy Needs Escort Carriers
snippet: “When word of crisis breaks out in Washington, it’s no accident that the first question that comes to everyone’s lips is, where is the nearest carrier?” President Bill Clinton said that to the crew of the USS Theodore Roosevelt in 1993, but it’s just as true today. Aircraft carriers have long played a crucial role in our Navy’s ability to project power globally. But they must adapt as threats and technology change. To fight China, the U.S. Navy will need more air power at sea, given the susceptibility of fixed airfields to missile strikes and the limited number of logistics and resupply ships available to sustain those bases under threat. This point has been made explicit with the evacuation under missile attack of the Fifth Fleet’s headquarters in Bahrain during the current conflict with Iran. title: Governor Sarah Huckabee Sanders and Derrick Morgan on Clarity and Conviction in a World Gone Crazy
snippet: Join Heritage Foundation Executive Vice President Derrick Morgan for a conversation with Sarah Huckabee Sanders , governor of Arkansas and former White House press secretary, on her forthcoming book, Unapologetic: Clarity and Conviction in a World Gone Crazy . As political, cultural, and social institutions face growing public skepticism, Sanders argues that effective leadership begins with the courage to stand firmly on principle. Drawing from her experiences at the center of national politics, her historic election as Arkansas’ first female governor, and the personal trials that have shaped her life, Sanders offers a candid reflection on faith, resilience, and public service. Don’t miss this exploration of what it means to lead with conviction, challenge the status quo, and advance enduring values in an increasingly turbulent age.
